overview: Heart valve disease occurs when one or more of the four heart valves do not function properly. The affected valve may become narrowed, fail to close completely, become floppy, or be improperly formed. These abnormalities alter normal blood flow through the heart and can eventually affect circulation throughout the body. Heart valve disease may involve the aortic, mitral, tricuspid, or pulmonary valves and can be congenital or acquired later in life.
ecg_limitations: ecg alone cannot diagnose valvular heart disease

history_questions: Do you experience shortness of breath during activity or at rest?
Do you become tired more easily than before?
Do you feel irregular or rapid heartbeats?
Do your symptoms worsen during physical activity?
Have you ever been diagnosed with rheumatic fever?
Have you previously been told you have a heart murmur or valve problem?

followup_questions.shortness_of_breath: Do you experience shortness of breath during activity, rest, or while lying down?
followup_questions.fatigue: Have you noticed increasing fatigue during daily activities?
followup_questions.chest_pain: Do you experience chest pain or chest pressure?
followup_questions.palpitations: Do you feel irregular or rapid heartbeats?
followup_questions.syncope: Have you fainted or nearly fainted?
followup_questions.heart_murmur: Have you ever been told you have a heart murmur?
followup_questions.history_of_rheumatic_fever: Have you ever had rheumatic fever?
followup_questions.known_valve_disease: Have you previously been diagnosed with a heart valve problem?
followup_questions.echocardiogram_result: Have you had an echocardiogram and were any valve abnormalities reported?

confidence_rules: history of rheumatic fever increases suspicion
progressive shortness of breath increases suspicion
atrial fibrillation may support advanced valve disease
agent_reasoning_hints: echocardiography is the primary diagnostic modality
ecg findings alone are insufficient for diagnosis
severity depends on valve anatomy and blood flow abnormalities
atrial fibrillation is a common complication
heart failure symptoms may indicate advanced disease
some patients remain asymptomatic for years
source_notes: heart valve disease may affect any of the four cardiac valves
major valve abnormalities include stenosis, regurgitation, prolapse and atresia
surgery may be required even before severe symptoms occur
heart failure and atrial fibrillation are important complications
